title: Etaleness along a closed subscheme from its infinitesimal neighbourhoods
statement: Let $g:X\to S$ be a morphism of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] between locally Noetherian schemes [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Let $Z\subseteq S$ be a closed subscheme with quasi-coherent ideal sheaf $\mathcal J$, let $Z_n\subseteq S$ be its $n$-th infinitesimal neighbourhood, the closed subscheme cut out by $\mathcal J^{n+1}$ [def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers], and $X_n=Z_n\times_SX$ [def-pc-base-change]. If $X_n\to Z_n$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism] for every $n\ge0$, then $g$ is etale at every point of $g^{-1}(Z)$: there is an open subscheme $W\subseteq X$ containing $g^{-1}(Z)$ such that $g|_W:W\to S$ is etale.

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma 0A43 (label lemma-check-smoothness-on-infinitesimal-nbhds), part (2), with its proof via Lemma lemma-lifting-along-artinian-at-point (Artinian infinitesimal lifting criterion at a point); etale at a point as in Morphisms, Definition 02GI

mathlib_searches.query: if X x_S S_n -> S_n is etale for all infinitesimal neighbourhoods S_n of a closed subscheme then X -> S is etale near the fibre
